title: Learning with Rejection
authors: Corinna Cortes, Giulia DeSalvo, Mehryar Mohri
venue: International Conference on Algorithmic Learning Theory (ALT), Lecture Notes in Computer Science vol. 9925, Springer
conclusions: Introduces a general framework for classification with a rejection option that jointly learns two functions: a predictor h and a rejection function r, generalizing prior confidence-based (threshold-on-h) rejection.

Rejection incurs a fixed, pre-specified per-instance cost c (constant cost model); an incorrect non-rejected prediction costs 1, a correct one costs 0 -- this is an instance-level pricing scheme with no global budget on how many points may be rejected.

Derives data-dependent (Rademacher-complexity) generalization bounds for the (h,r) pair, two convex surrogate losses (Max Hinge, Plus Hinge) that are shown calibrated and (H,R)-consistent, and margin-based learning guarantees used to build kernel-based QP algorithms (CHR).
Empirically, the CHR algorithms outperform the prior double-hinge-loss (DHL) rejection baseline on 7 UCI datasets across a range of rejection costs c.

Conclusion explicitly flags a rejection-fraction/count constraint as unaddressed future work: 'a natural extension of our framework is to include a constraint on the maximum fraction of points that can be rejected. Such an additional constraint will require new algorithms and generalization bounds' -- confirming the paper has no count/budget guarantee.
